nodes.name: NiFeCr electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam (NF, 110 ppi, 1.0 mm thickness, exposed geometric area: 1.0 × 1.0 cm²) was used as the working electrode (coating substrate). The counter and reference electrodes were a graphite plate and Ag/AgCl (1.0 M KCl, CHI-111), respectively. The electrodeposition was carried out at an applied potential of -1.0 V vs. Ag/AgCl for 900 s, in an electrodeposition bath containing 12 mM nickel nitrate hexahydrate (99.5%, Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, Chem Supply), 3 mM iron nitrate nonahydrate (99.5%, Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, Chem Supply) and 6 mM chromium nitrate nonahydrate (99.5%, Cr(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, Jax Chemicals). During the electrodeposition process, locally generated OH⁻ ions via the reduction of nitrate aqueous solution react with Ni²⁺, Fe³⁺ and/or Cr³⁺, and co-precipitate onto the substrate (i.e. NF), forming a light-brown colored coating (denoted as NiFeCr/NF). Thereafter the electrodeposited electrode was thoroughly rinsed with water and air-dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeCr/NF shows more M–OH bonds (531.9 eV) than NiFe/NF; Fe3+ and Ni2+ oxidation states in both; Cr3+ in NiFeCr/NF; Ni/Fe peaks shift +0.3 eV in NiFeCr/NF indicating electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the O1s XPS data (Fig. 1a), one dominant peak can be fitted into three sub-peaks... NiFeCr/NF contains more M–OH bonds for the hydroxide while the NiFe/NF control sample has more M–O bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeCr (oxy)hydroxide shows small clusters of atoms without clear lattice fringes and amorphous nature confirmed by SAED halo pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1e shows that the NiFeCr compound consists of small clusters of atoms without clear lattice fringes, indicating the amorphous nature of the catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni:Fe:Cr ratio of 6:1:2 in NiFeCr/NF and Ni:Fe ratio of 3:2 in NiFe/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Considering the above analysis, a Ni : Fe ratio of 3 : 2 in NiFe/NF and a Ni : Fe : Cr ratio of 6 : 1 : 2 in NiFeCr/NF are obtained, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe catalyst shows Ni–O doublet peaks shifting to ~475 and ~555 cm⁻¹ indicating β-NiOOH formation; NiFeCr shows stronger ~555 cm⁻¹ peak indicating more β-NiOOH phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the applied potential reaches 0.5 V or higher, the doublet Ni–O peaks (400–600 cm⁻¹) shift gradually to ~475 and ~555 cm⁻¹, attributed to Ni–O vibrations in the NiOOH intermediate.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe catalyst transforms to Fe-substituted-β-NiOOH with shorter Fe–O bonds (active site); NiFeCr catalyst shows Cr oxidized to 6+ with Cr–O bond at 1.2 Å (active site) in Cr,Fe-substituted-β-NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At an applied potential of 0.70 V (black curves in Fig. 4f and g), the FT peaks of both Fe and Ni shift in the lower R′ direction, indicating the formation of shorter Fe–O and Ni–O bonds... for the Cr FT in the NiFeCr catalyst (Fig. 4h), the peak of Cr–O in the 1st shell shifts negatively with a dominant peak at 1.2 Å.
